decisions.choice: a new speech, given in the plains of Moab before Israel crosses the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel is still camped in the plains of Moab across from Jericho (33:48-50; 36:13). The last speech ended with the command to drive out the people of Canaan and divide the land by lot (33:50-56). This one sets out the borders of that land (verses 1-15) and names the men who will divide it (verses 16-29).

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("parla", "commanda"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit")
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Pentateuch: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé that of spoken and school French.

records.literal_gloss: Command [the] sons of Israel and say to them, When you [are] coming into the land [of] Canaan, this [is] the land that will fall to you as an inheritance, [the] land of Canaan by its borders,

en.B: "Give the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this command and tell them: 'You are about to enter the land of Canaan. Here is the land that will fall to you as your inheritance, the land of Canaan with these borders:

sw.L: "Waamuru wana wa Israeli na uwaambie, 'Mtakapoingia katika nchi ya Kanaani, hii [ndiyo] nchi itakayowaangukia kuwa urithi, nchi ya Kanaani kwa mipaka yake:

vi.L: "Hãy truyền cho con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên và nói với họ: 'Khi các ngươi vào xứ Ca-na-an, thì đây [là] xứ sẽ rơi vào [phần] các ngươi làm sản nghiệp, tức là xứ Ca-na-an theo các ranh giới của nó:
vi.B: "Con hãy truyền lệnh này cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và bảo họ: 'Các ngươi sắp vào xứ Ca-na-an. Đây là xứ sẽ được bắt thăm chia cho các ngươi làm sản nghiệp, tức là xứ Ca-na-an với những ranh giới sau đây:
vi.R: "Con hãy truyền dặn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Hãy bảo họ: 'Các ngươi sắp vào xứ Ca-na-an. Xứ ấy sẽ được chia cho các ngươi bằng cách bắt thăm, để làm đất riêng của các ngươi. Đây là ranh giới của xứ ấy.

ko.L: "이스라엘 자손에게 명령하고 그들에게 일러라. '너희가 가나안 땅으로 들어갈 때, 이것이 너희에게 유산으로 떨어질 땅, 곧 그 경계대로의 가나안 땅이다.
ko.B: "이스라엘 백성에게 이렇게 명령하여 일러라. '너희는 이제 곧 가나안 땅으로 들어간다. 너희에게 유산으로 돌아갈 땅, 곧 가나안 땅의 경계는 이러하다.

pt.L: "Ordena aos filhos de Israel e dize-lhes: 'Quando vocês entrarem na terra de Canaã, esta [é] a terra que cairá para vocês como herança, a terra de Canaã segundo as suas fronteiras:
pt.B: "Dá esta ordem aos israelitas e dize-lhes: 'Vocês estão para entrar na terra de Canaã. Esta é a terra que lhes caberá como herança, a terra de Canaã com estas fronteiras:
pt.R: "Dá estas ordens aos israelitas. Diz a eles: 'Logo vocês vão entrar na terra de Canaã. Esta é a terra que vocês vão receber por sorteio, para ser de vocês. Estas são as fronteiras dela.

decisions.choice: you are coming: you are about to enter
decisions.reason: The verb form describes something happening now or about to happen. Israel has not yet crossed the Jordan; the borders are given ahead of time, as the laws of 33:51 and 35:10 are.

decisions.choice: will fall to you: will come to you by lot
decisions.reason: Land is said to "fall" to someone because it was shared out by casting lots (verse 13; 26:55-56; Joshua 17:5). The land is not taken by Israel's own choice; it is given to them.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a share of land held for good and handed down in the family
decisions.reason: The word means a possession that belongs to a family or tribe and passes from parents to children. The land is Israel's inheritance because the LORD gives it to them, as he promised their ancestors (Genesis 15:18; Exodus 6:8).

decisions.choice: will be given to you by lot to be your own
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of land "falling" to someone (m2) and what an inheritance is (m3).

decisions.choice: les caerá en herencia (L), les tocará en herencia (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of land "falling" to someone; Balanced uses "tocar", the ordinary verb for what falls to someone in a draw.

decisions.choice: qui vous écherra (L), qui vous reviendra (B)
decisions.reason: "Échoir" is the French verb for a share that falls to someone, as by lot, and keeps the Hebrew picture at Literal; Balanced uses the everyday "revenir".

decisions.choice: itakayowaangukia (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Kuangukia" keeps the Hebrew picture of a share falling to someone by lot and is natural Swahili for a share that comes to someone.

decisions.choice: God addresses Moses as "ngươi" at L and "con" at B and R; the command Moses passes on speaks to Israel as "các ngươi" at every level
alternatives: "các con" for Israel at B and R
decisions.reason: As in Genesis, Exodus and the earlier chapters of Numbers: "con" carries the closeness of God speaking to Moses in modern Vietnamese, while the laws for the whole people keep the formal "các ngươi" the term sheet sets for God's commands.

decisions.choice: "rơi vào [phần] các ngươi làm sản nghiệp" (L), "được bắt thăm chia cho các ngươi làm sản nghiệp" (B), "được chia ... bằng cách bắt thăm, để làm đất riêng" (R)
decisions.reason: "sản nghiệp" is the word for a family's lasting inheritance used through Numbers; L keeps the picture of the lot "falling", B and R say plainly that the land is shared out by lot, and R says "đất riêng" (land of your own) for new readers.

decisions.choice: God's instructions to Moses, and the words Moses is to pass on to Israel, in the plain style (해라체) with "너" / "너희": "-하라", "-하여라" at Literal and Balanced, "-해야 한다", "-하면 안 된다" at Readable; "이스라엘 자손" (L), "이스라엘 백성" (B), "이스라엘 사람들" (R) with no gender span
alternatives: 합쇼체 for the words to the people
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Exodus to Deuteronomy sets God's commands, and as Numbers 1-19 already read in Korean. The Korean words for the people already include women and men, so the English gender setting has nothing to change. Recorded once for Numbers 34-36.

decisions.choice: "유산으로 떨어질" (L); "유산으로 돌아갈" (B); "제비를 뽑아 ... 너희 것이 되게 할" (R); "유산" for the inheritance
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of land "falling" to someone by lot; Balanced says it plainly, and Readable explains the lot, as the meaning decision does. "유산" is the word Joshua already uses for the tribes' land; the older church word "기업" now means a business. Recorded once for Numbers 34-36.

decisions.choice: cairá para vocês (L); lhes caberá (B); vão receber por sorteio (R)
decisions.reason: Land "falls" to someone because it was shared out by lot (m2). Literal keeps the Hebrew verb, "cair", which Portuguese can say of a lot; Balanced says "caber", the ordinary Portuguese verb for what falls to someone as their share ("caber em sorte"); Readable says it plainly with "por sorteio", as the English Readable says "by lot". God speaks to Moses with "tu" ("Ordena", "dize-lhes"); the words Moses passes on address the people as "vocês".

records.literal_gloss: And will be for you [the] side [of the] south from [the] wilderness of Zin along [the] hands of Edom, and will be for you [the] border [of the] south from [the] end of [the] Sea of the Salt eastward,

en.B: Your southern side will take in the wilderness of Zin, alongside Edom. On the east, your southern border will start at the end of the Dead Sea.
en.R: In the south, your land will include the Zin Desert, next to the land of Edom. The southern border will begin in the east, at the southern tip of the Dead Sea.

fr.L: votre côté sud ira du désert de Tsin, le long d’Édom, et votre frontière sud partira de l’extrémité de la mer Salée, à l’est.
fr.B: Votre côté sud englobera le désert de Tsin, le long d’Édom. À l’est, votre frontière sud commencera à l’extrémité de la mer Morte.
fr.R: Au sud, votre pays comprendra le désert de Tsin, à côté du pays d’Édom. La frontière sud commencera à l’est, à la pointe sud de la mer Morte.

sw.L: upande wenu wa kusini utakuwa tangu nyika ya Zini kando ya Edomu, na mpaka wenu wa kusini utaanzia mwisho wa Bahari ya Chumvi upande wa mashariki.
sw.B: Upande wenu wa kusini utajumuisha nyika ya Zini, kando ya Edomu. Upande wa mashariki, mpaka wenu wa kusini utaanzia mwisho wa Bahari Mfu.
sw.R: Upande wa kusini, nchi yenu itajumuisha jangwa la Zini, karibu na nchi ya Edomu. Mpaka wa kusini utaanzia mashariki, kwenye ncha ya kusini ya Bahari Mfu.

vi.L: Phía nam của các ngươi sẽ là từ hoang mạc Xin dọc theo phía Ê-đôm; và ranh giới phía nam của các ngươi sẽ là từ cuối Biển Muối về phía đông.
vi.B: Phía nam của các ngươi sẽ gồm hoang mạc Xin, dọc theo Ê-đôm. Ở phía đông, ranh giới phía nam của các ngươi sẽ bắt đầu từ cuối Biển Chết.
vi.R: Ở phía nam, đất của các ngươi sẽ gồm cả hoang mạc Xin, sát bên xứ Ê-đôm. Ranh giới phía nam sẽ bắt đầu ở phía đông, tại mũi phía nam của Biển Chết.

ko.L: 너희의 남쪽 면은 신 광야에서부터 에돔 곁을 따라 [이어질] 것이요, 너희의 남쪽 경계는 동쪽으로 염해 끝에서부터 [시작될] 것이다.
ko.B: 너희 땅의 남쪽은 에돔과 맞닿은 신 광야를 포함한다. 남쪽 경계는 동쪽 사해 끝에서 시작된다.
ko.R: 남쪽으로는 에돔 땅 옆에 있는 신 광야가 너희 땅에 들어간다. 남쪽 경계는 동쪽에서 사해의 남쪽 끝에서부터 시작된다.

pt.L: o lado sul de vocês será desde o deserto de Zim, ao longo do lado de Edom, e a fronteira sul de vocês será desde a extremidade do mar Salgado, a leste.
pt.B: O lado sul de vocês incluirá o deserto de Zim, junto a Edom. A leste, a fronteira sul de vocês começará na extremidade do mar Morto.
pt.R: No sul, a terra de vocês vai incluir o deserto de Zim, ao lado da terra de Edom. A fronteira sul vai começar no leste, na ponta sul do mar Morto.

decisions.choice: the four borders, given in order: south, west, north, east
decisions.reason: The chapter traces the land's edges one side at a time: south (verses 3-5), west (verse 6), north (verses 7-9) and east (verses 10-12). The same southern line marks the edge of Judah in Joshua 15:1-4, and Ezekiel's picture of the land in the age to come uses much of the northern and eastern line (Ezekiel 47:15-20). The land described is Canaan west of the Jordan; it does not include the land east of the river (verses 14-15).

decisions.choice: along the hands of Edom: alongside Edom's territory
decisions.reason: "Hands" here means sides or edges, as in a place lying "at the hand of" another. The wilderness of Zin runs beside the land of Edom, which lay to the south-east (20:16, 23).

decisions.choice: the Salt Sea: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The Salt Sea is the Dead Sea, as in Genesis 14:3. The border starts at its southern end and runs west.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea; the Zin Desert (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the modern name for the Salt Sea, as in Genesis 14:3; Literal keeps "Salt Sea". Readable calls the wilderness of Zin "the Zin Desert", as in 13:21.

decisions.choice: the southern tip
decisions.reason: The end of the sea from which a southern border runs west must be its southern end. Readable says so; Literal and Balanced keep "the end".

decisions.choice: "Biển Muối" (L), "Biển Chết" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Joshua 15:2-5 in Vietnamese: L keeps the Hebrew name, B and R use the name Vietnamese readers know from maps.

decisions.choice: "염해" (L); "사해" (B, R) for the Salt Sea; "신 광야" at every level
decisions.reason: As Joshua 15:2 in Korean: Literal keeps the Hebrew name, Balanced and Readable give the name Korean readers know (meaning decision). "광야" stays at Readable too, as in Numbers 1:1, though the English Readable says "Desert".

decisions.choice: o mar Salgado (L); o mar Morto (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as Genesis 14:3 has it in Portuguese: Literal keeps the Hebrew name, "o mar Salgado", and Balanced and Readable use the name the reader knows, "o mar Morto" (m3), as the English does. "Mar" is lowercase before the name, as in "o mar Vermelho".

source.text: וְנָסַ֣ב לָכֶם֩ הַגְּב֨וּל מִנֶּ֜גֶב לְמַעֲלֵ֤ה עַקְרַבִּים֙ וְעָ֣בַר צִ֔נָה וְהָיוּ֙ תּֽוֹצְאֹתָ֔יו מִנֶּ֖גֶב לְקָדֵ֣שׁ בַּרְנֵ֑עַ וְיָצָ֥א חֲצַר־אַדָּ֖ר וְעָבַ֥ר עַצְמֹֽנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will turn for you the border from [the] south to [the] ascent of Akrabbim, and will pass on to Zin, and will be its goings out from [the] south to Kadesh-barnea, and will go out [to] Hazar-addar, and will pass on to Azmon,

en.L: And the border will turn for you south of the ascent of Akrabbim and pass on to Zin, and its end will be south of Kadesh-barnea; and it will go out to Hazar-addar and pass on to Azmon.
en.B: From there your border will turn and run south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and on to Zin, reaching as far as the south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go out to Hazar-addar and on to Azmon.
en.R: From there it will turn and pass south of Scorpion Pass and go on through Zin. Its farthest point will be south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go on to Hazar-addar and over to Azmon.

es.L: Y la frontera {{plural_you:les|os}} girará al sur de la subida de Acrabim y pasará hasta Zin, y su término estará al sur de Cades-barnea; y saldrá a Hazar-adar y pasará a Azmón.
es.B: Desde allí {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera girará y pasará al sur de la Subida de Acrabim, seguirá hasta Zin y llegará hasta el sur de Cades-barnea. Luego saldrá hacia Hazar-adar y seguirá hasta Azmón.
es.R: Desde allí girará y pasará al sur del Paso de los Escorpiones, y seguirá por Zin. Su punto más lejano estará al sur de Cades-barnea. Luego seguirá hasta Hazar-adar y llegará a Azmón.

fr.L: Et la frontière tournera pour vous au sud de la montée d’Akrabbim et passera vers Tsin, et son aboutissement sera au sud de Kadesh-Barnéa ; puis elle sortira vers Hatsar-Addar et passera vers Atsmon.
fr.B: De là, votre frontière tournera et passera au sud de la Montée d’Akrabbim, puis jusqu’à Tsin, et elle descendra jusqu’au sud de Kadesh-Barnéa. Ensuite elle ira vers Hatsar-Addar et continuera jusqu’à Atsmon.
fr.R: De là, elle tournera et passera au sud du col des Scorpions, puis elle traversera Tsin. Son point le plus éloigné se trouvera au sud de Kadesh-Barnéa. Ensuite elle ira jusqu’à Hatsar-Addar, puis jusqu’à Atsmon.

sw.L: Na mpaka wenu utageuka kusini mwa mwinuko wa Akrabimu, na kupita hadi Zini, na miisho yake itakuwa kusini mwa Kadesh-barnea; nao utatokea Hasar-adari na kupita hadi Asmoni.
sw.B: Kutoka hapo mpaka wenu utageuka na kupita kusini mwa Mwinuko wa Akrabimu, kisha hadi Zini, na kufika upande wa kusini wa Kadesh-barnea. Kisha utaendelea hadi Hasar-adari na kufika Asmoni.
sw.R: Kutoka hapo utageuka na kupita kusini mwa Kipito cha Nge, kisha utapitia Zini. Sehemu yake ya mbali kabisa itakuwa kusini mwa Kadesh-barnea. Kisha utaendelea hadi Hasar-adari na kufika Asmoni.

vi.L: Và ranh giới sẽ vòng cho các ngươi về phía nam dốc Ạc-ráp-bim, và đi qua Xin, và điểm cuối của nó sẽ ở phía nam Ca-đe-Ba-nê-a; rồi nó sẽ đi ra đến Hát-sa-Át-đa và đi qua Át-môn.
vi.B: Từ đó ranh giới của các ngươi sẽ vòng xuống, chạy về phía nam dốc Ạc-ráp-bim, qua Xin, và đến tận phía nam Ca-đe-Ba-nê-a. Rồi nó sẽ đi ra đến Hát-sa-Át-đa và tiếp đến Át-môn.
vi.R: Từ đó ranh giới sẽ vòng xuống, đi qua phía nam đèo Bọ Cạp và tiếp tục qua Xin. Điểm xa nhất của nó sẽ ở phía nam Ca-đe-Ba-nê-a. Rồi nó sẽ đi đến Hát-sa-Át-đa và sang Át-môn.

ko.L: 그리고 그 경계는 너희를 위하여 아그랍빔 비탈 남쪽으로 돌아 신으로 지나가고, 그 끝은 가데스 바네아 남쪽이 될 것이다. 또 하살아달로 나가서 아스몬으로 지나갈 것이다.
ko.B: 거기에서 너희 경계는 돌아서 아그랍빔 고개 남쪽을 지나 신에 이르고, 가데스 바네아 남쪽까지 뻗을 것이다. 그리고 하살아달로 나가서 아스몬에 이를 것이다.
ko.R: 거기에서 경계는 돌아서 전갈 고개 남쪽을 지나 신으로 간다. 가장 남쪽은 가데스 바네아의 남쪽이다. 그다음에 하살아달로 나가서 아스몬까지 간다.

pt.L: E a fronteira de vocês dará a volta ao sul da subida de Acrabim, e passará a Zim, e o seu extremo será ao sul de Cades-Barneia; e sairá a Hazar-Adar e passará a Azmom.
pt.B: Dali a fronteira de vocês fará uma curva e passará ao sul da Subida de Acrabim, seguindo até Zim e chegando até o sul de Cades-Barneia. Depois irá até Hazar-Adar e seguirá até Azmom.
pt.R: Dali ela vai virar e passar ao sul da Subida dos Escorpiões, e seguir através de Zim. O seu ponto mais distante vai ser ao sul de Cades-Barneia. Depois ela vai seguir até Hazar-Adar e até Azmom.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Akrabbim: the Scorpions' Pass
decisions.reason: Akrabbim means "scorpions", and the "ascent" is a road climbing up a steep slope. It was a pass going up from the desert south-west of the Dead Sea into the hills (Joshua 15:3; Judges 1:36).

decisions.choice: its goings out: the point the border reaches
decisions.reason: The plural word means the places where something goes out to, its farthest reach or end. It is used of each border in this chapter (verses 5, 8, 9, 12). Here, in the middle of the line, it marks how far south the border dips, below Kadesh-barnea.

decisions.choice: they will be: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) read "it will be"; the reading the scribes marked (qere), followed here, is "they will be", agreeing with the plural "its goings out". The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: Kadesh-barnea, Hazar-addar, Azmon: places on the southern edge
decisions.reason: Kadesh-barnea is the oasis where Israel camped for a long time and from which the scouts were sent (13:26; 20:1; 32:8). Hazar-addar and Azmon lay between Kadesh and the Wadi of Egypt; where exactly is not known. Joshua 15:3-4 traces the same line, with Hezron and Addar for Hazar-addar.

decisions.choice: the Ascent of Akrabbim (B); Scorpion Pass (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the place name as a name; Readable says what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: the border places transcribed by the book's conventions: "ts" for tsade ("Hatsar-Addar", "Atsmon", "Tsin")
decisions.reason: Names with no established French form are transcribed as elsewhere in Numbers, so that the same Hebrew letters come out the same way.

decisions.choice: "dốc Ạc-ráp-bim" (L, B), "đèo Bọ Cạp" (R); "Ca-đe-Ba-nê-a"
decisions.reason: The pass follows Joshua 15:3 in Vietnamese. The town is spelled with "Ca-đe", the form the term sheet and Numbers 13-27 use for Kadesh, so that the two names visibly belong together; Joshua spells it "Ca-đê-Ba-nê-a", and a reviewer should make the books agree.

decisions.choice: "아그랍빔 비탈" (L); "아그랍빔 고개" (B); "전갈 고개" (R); "가데스 바네아", "하살아달", "아스몬"
decisions.reason: The same forms as Joshua 15:3-4 in Korean: Literal and Balanced keep the name, Readable says what it means, the Scorpions' Pass (meaning decision). The other names are the usual Protestant forms.

decisions.choice: a subida de Acrabim (L), a Subida de Acrabim (B), a Subida dos Escorpiões (R); Cades-Barneia, Hazar-Adar, Azmom
decisions.reason: The usual Brazilian forms of the names, as at 13:21: "c" for k, a final -on written "-om", the two parts of a compound name each capitalised, as "Lebo-Hamate". "Subida" is the Portuguese word for a road climbing a slope (m1); Readable says what Akrabbim means, as the English Readable does, and keeps the word "Subida" so that the name still reads as a place.

source.text: וְנָסַ֧ב הַגְּב֛וּל מֵעַצְמ֖וֹן נַ֣חְלָה מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהָי֥וּ תוֹצְאֹתָ֖יו הַיָּֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will turn the border from Azmon [to the] wadi of Egypt, and will be its goings out at the sea.

en.L: And the border will turn from Azmon to the brook of Egypt, and its end will be at the sea.
en.B: From Azmon the border will bend around to the Wadi of Egypt and end at the sea.
en.R: At Azmon it will turn toward the Wadi of Egypt, a stream that is dry most of the year. It will end at the Mediterranean Sea.

es.L: Y la frontera girará desde Azmón hasta el torrente de Egipto, y su término estará en el mar.
es.B: Desde Azmón la frontera se curvará hacia el Torrente de Egipto y terminará en el mar.
es.R: En Azmón girará hacia el Torrente de Egipto, un cauce que está seco casi todo el año. Terminará en el mar Mediterráneo.

fr.L: Et la frontière tournera depuis Atsmon vers le torrent d’Égypte, et son aboutissement sera à la mer.
fr.B: Depuis Atsmon, la frontière s’incurvera vers le Torrent d’Égypte et se terminera à la mer.
fr.R: À Atsmon, elle tournera vers le Torrent d’Égypte, un cours d’eau à sec presque toute l’année. Elle se terminera à la mer Méditerranée.

sw.L: Na mpaka utageuka kutoka Asmoni hadi kijito cha Misri, na miisho yake itakuwa baharini.
sw.B: Kutoka Asmoni mpaka utapinda kuelekea Kijito cha Misri na kuishia baharini.
sw.R: Huko Asmoni utageuka kuelekea Kijito cha Misri, mto ambao hukauka karibu mwaka mzima. Utaishia kwenye Bahari ya Mediterania.

vi.L: Và ranh giới sẽ vòng từ Át-môn đến suối Ai Cập, và điểm cuối của nó sẽ ở biển.
vi.B: Từ Át-môn ranh giới sẽ uốn về phía khe Ai Cập và dừng lại ở biển.
vi.R: Tại Át-môn, nó sẽ quay về phía khe Ai Cập, một dòng suối khô cạn gần như quanh năm. Ranh giới sẽ dừng lại ở Địa Trung Hải.

ko.L: 그리고 그 경계는 아스몬에서 이집트 시내로 돌아가고, 그 끝은 바다가 될 것이다.
ko.B: 경계는 아스몬에서 이집트 시내 쪽으로 굽어 돌아 바다에서 끝날 것이다.
ko.R: 아스몬에서 경계는 이집트 시내 쪽으로 돈다. 그 시내는 한 해의 대부분 말라 있는 시냇바닥이다. 경계는 지중해에서 끝난다.

pt.L: E a fronteira dará a volta desde Azmom até o ribeiro do Egito, e o seu extremo será no mar.
pt.B: De Azmom a fronteira fará uma curva até o ribeiro do Egito e terminará no mar.
pt.R: Em Azmom, ela vai virar em direção ao ribeiro do Egito, um riacho que fica seco a maior parte do ano. Ela vai terminar no mar Mediterrâneo.

decisions.choice: the wadi of Egypt: the stream bed between Canaan and Egypt
decisions.reason: The word means a valley with a stream that flows only in the rainy season. The Wadi of Egypt marked the edge of Canaan toward Egypt, in the desert of northern Sinai (Joshua 15:4, 47; 1 Kings 8:65; Isaiah 27:12). It is not the Nile, which is called by a different word.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: The southern border runs west to the coast of the Great Sea, which forms the western border (verse 6).

decisions.choice: brook (L), Wadi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the common English word "brook". Balanced and Readable use "wadi", the word for a dry stream bed in this part of the world, as the name of the place; Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable names the sea (m2).

decisions.choice: el torrente de Egipto (L), el Torrente de Egipto as a name (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Torrente" is the ordinary Spanish word for a stream bed that carries water only in the rains; "uadi" is rare. Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: le torrent d'Égypte (L), le Torrent d'Égypte as a name (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Torrent" is the usual French word for a stream that runs only after rain; "oued" is exact but regional. Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kijito cha Misri (L), Kijito cha Misri as a name (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Kijito" is the word used for a wadi elsewhere in the Pentateuch drafts (Deuteronomy 2); Readable explains that it is dry most of the year.

decisions.choice: "suối Ai Cập" (L), "khe Ai Cập" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Joshua 15:4 and Kings in Vietnamese: "khe" is a stream bed that runs only in the rains, which is what a wadi is; "sông" would suggest the Nile.

decisions.choice: "이집트 시내"; "바다" (L, B), "지중해" (R)
decisions.reason: As Joshua 15:4 in Korean: a wadi runs only after rain (meaning decision), so "시내" rather than "강"; Readable says what it is and names the Mediterranean, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: o ribeiro do Egito (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book. Portuguese has no everyday word for a wadi: "uádi" is rare, and "rio" would suggest the Nile, which m1 rules out. "Ribeiro" is a small stream, the word Genesis 32:24 uses in Portuguese for the Jabbok, so it serves at every level where the English moves from "brook" to "Wadi"; Readable explains that it is dry most of the year, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וּגְב֣וּל יָ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם הַיָּ֥ם הַגָּד֖וֹל וּגְב֑וּל זֶֽה־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֥וּל יָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] border [of the] west: and will be for you the Sea the Great and [its] border; this will be for you [the] border [of the] west.

en.L: And [as for] the western border, the Great Sea and [its] coast will be [the border] for you; this will be your western border.
en.B: Your western border will be the Great Sea and its coast. That will be your border on the west.
en.R: In the west, the border will be the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. That will be your western border.

es.L: Y [en cuanto a] la frontera occidental, el mar Grande y [su] costa {{plural_you:les|os}} servirán [de frontera]; esta será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera occidental.
es.B: {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} frontera occidental será el mar Grande y su costa. Esa será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera al oeste.
es.R: Al oeste, la frontera será la costa del mar Mediterráneo. Esa será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera occidental.

fr.L: Et [quant à] la frontière de l’ouest, la Grande Mer et [sa] côte seront [la frontière] pour vous ; ce sera votre frontière de l’ouest.
fr.B: Votre frontière ouest sera la Grande Mer et son rivage. Ce sera votre frontière à l’ouest.
fr.R: À l’ouest, la frontière sera la côte de la mer Méditerranée. Ce sera votre frontière ouest.

sw.L: Na [kuhusu] mpaka wa magharibi, Bahari Kuu na pwani [yake] itakuwa [mpaka] kwenu; huu utakuwa mpaka wenu wa magharibi.
sw.B: Mpaka wenu wa magharibi utakuwa Bahari Kuu na pwani yake. Huo ndio utakaokuwa mpaka wenu upande wa magharibi.
sw.R: Upande wa magharibi, mpaka utakuwa pwani ya Bahari ya Mediterania. Huo ndio mpaka wenu wa magharibi.

vi.L: Và [về] ranh giới phía tây, Biển Lớn và bờ [của nó] sẽ là [ranh giới] cho các ngươi; đây sẽ là ranh giới phía tây của các ngươi.
vi.B: Ranh giới phía tây của các ngươi sẽ là Biển Lớn và bờ biển. Đó sẽ là ranh giới phía tây của các ngươi.
vi.R: Ở phía tây, ranh giới sẽ là bờ Địa Trung Hải. Đó là ranh giới phía tây của các ngươi.

ko.L: 그리고 서쪽 경계[로 말하면], 대해와 [그] 해안이 너희에게 [경계가] 될 것이다. 이것이 너희의 서쪽 경계가 될 것이다.
ko.B: 너희의 서쪽 경계는 대해와 그 해안이다. 이것이 너희의 서쪽 경계가 될 것이다.
ko.R: 서쪽 경계는 지중해 바닷가이다. 이것이 너희 땅의 서쪽 경계이다.

pt.L: E [quanto à] fronteira ocidental, o Grande Mar e [a sua] costa serão [a fronteira] para vocês; esta será a fronteira ocidental de vocês.
pt.B: A fronteira ocidental de vocês será o Grande Mar e a sua costa. Essa será a fronteira de vocês a oeste.
pt.R: No oeste, a fronteira vai ser a costa do mar Mediterrâneo. Essa vai ser a fronteira ocidental de vocês.

decisions.choice: the Great Sea: the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: The Great Sea is the Mediterranean, the sea along the whole western side of Canaan (Joshua 1:4; 15:12).

decisions.choice: west: literally "sea"
decisions.reason: The word for "west" is the word "sea", because the sea lay to the west of the land. Here the same word stands for both, with the sea itself as the western border.

decisions.choice: and its border: the coast
decisions.reason: The word "border" here means the edge of the sea, its coastline, which is the land's boundary on that side. Joshua 15:12 uses the same words for Judah's western border.

decisions.choice: [as for] ... [its] ... [the border]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew states the heading first, "the western border", then what it is. Literal supplies words so the clause can be read in English.

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable uses the modern name of the Great Sea (m1).

decisions.choice: "Biển Lớn" (L, B), "Địa Trung Hải" (R)
decisions.reason: As Joshua 15:12 in Vietnamese; R names the sea as a modern reader knows it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "대해" (L, B); "지중해" (R) for the Great Sea; "서쪽" for the Hebrew "sea" side
decisions.reason: As Joshua 15:12 in Korean. Korean has no use of "sea" for "west", so every level says "서쪽" (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: o Grande Mar (L, B); o mar Mediterrâneo (R); a costa
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "o Grande Mar" keeps the Hebrew name at Literal and Balanced with both words capitalised, as a name, and Readable says "o mar Mediterrâneo" (m1), as the English does. The "border" of the sea is its coastline (m3), "a costa".

source.text: וְזֶֽה־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֣וּל צָפ֑וֹן מִן־הַיָּם֙ הַגָּדֹ֔ל תְּתָא֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם הֹ֥ר הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And this will be for you [the] border [of the] north: from the Sea the Great you will mark out for yourselves Hor the mountain.

en.L: And this will be your northern border: from the Great Sea you will mark out for yourselves [a line to] Mount Hor.
en.B: This will be your northern border: from the Great Sea mark out a line to Mount Hor.
en.R: In the north, draw your border line from the Mediterranean Sea to Mount Hor.

es.L: Y esta será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera norte: desde el mar Grande {{plural_you:trazarán|trazaréis}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [una línea hasta] el monte Hor.
es.B: Esta será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera norte: desde el mar Grande {{plural_you:tracen|trazad}} una línea hasta el monte Hor.
es.R: Al norte, {{plural_you:tracen|trazad}} la línea de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera desde el mar Mediterráneo hasta el monte Hor.

fr.L: Et voici quelle sera pour vous la frontière du nord : depuis la Grande Mer, vous tracerez pour vous-mêmes [une ligne jusqu’au] mont Hor.
fr.B: Voici votre frontière nord : depuis la Grande Mer, tracez une ligne jusqu’au mont Hor.
fr.R: Au nord, tracez la ligne de votre frontière depuis la mer Méditerranée jusqu’au mont Hor.

sw.L: Na huu utakuwa mpaka wenu wa kaskazini: kutoka Bahari Kuu mtajipimia [mstari hadi] Mlima Hori.
sw.B: Huu utakuwa mpaka wenu wa kaskazini: kutoka Bahari Kuu pimeni mstari hadi Mlima Hori.
sw.R: Upande wa kaskazini, wekeni mstari wa mpaka wenu kuanzia Bahari ya Mediterania hadi Mlima Hori.

vi.L: Và đây sẽ là ranh giới phía bắc của các ngươi: từ Biển Lớn các ngươi sẽ vạch cho mình [một đường đến] núi Hô-rơ.
vi.B: Đây sẽ là ranh giới phía bắc của các ngươi: từ Biển Lớn hãy vạch một đường đến núi Hô-rơ.
vi.R: Ở phía bắc, hãy vạch đường ranh giới từ Địa Trung Hải đến núi Hô-rơ.

ko.L: 그리고 이것이 너희의 북쪽 경계가 될 것이다. 대해에서부터 호르 산까지 너희를 위하여 [선을] 그을 것이다.
ko.B: 너희의 북쪽 경계는 이러하다. 대해에서 호르 산까지 선을 그어라.
ko.R: 북쪽으로는 지중해에서 호르 산까지 경계선을 그어라.

pt.L: E esta será a fronteira norte de vocês: desde o Grande Mar vocês traçarão para si [uma linha até] o monte Hor.
pt.B: Esta será a fronteira norte de vocês: desde o Grande Mar, tracem uma linha até o monte Hor.
pt.R: No norte, tracem a linha da fronteira desde o mar Mediterrâneo até o monte Hor.

decisions.choice: you will mark out: draw a line
decisions.reason: The verb is rare; here and in verse 8 it means to mark out a boundary or draw a line from one point to the next. Verse 10 uses a similar verb in the same sense.

decisions.choice: Mount Hor: a mountain in the north, not the place where Aaron died
alternatives: the same Mount Hor as in 20:22
decisions.reason: This Mount Hor has the same name as the mountain on the edge of Edom where Aaron died (20:22-29; 33:37-39), but it lies on the northern border, somewhere between the coast and Lebo-hamath, perhaps in the mountains of Lebanon. Which peak it was is not known.

decisions.choice: [a line to] (L), a line to (B), draw your border line (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "you will mark out Mount Hor". English needs "a line to" to make sense of it; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: "vạch" (mark out a line)
decisions.reason: "vạch" is the ordinary word for drawing a boundary line on the ground or on a map; it is used for the same verb in verses 8 and 10.

decisions.choice: "호르 산", the same Korean name as the mountain where Aaron died (20:22)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the same name; the meaning decision's footnote says it is a different mountain in the north, so Korean keeps the name and leaves the explanation to the footnote.

decisions.choice: traçar (uma linha)
decisions.reason: The verb means marking out a boundary from one point to the next (m1), here and in verses 8 and 10. "Traçar uma linha" is how Portuguese says it of a border; "demarcar" would need the whole border as its object, which the Hebrew does not give. Balanced and Readable use the plural imperative, "tracem", since "you" is the people (m3 at verse 18).

source.text: מֵהֹ֣ר הָהָ֔ר תְּתָא֖וּ לְבֹ֣א חֲמָ֑ת וְהָי֛וּ תּוֹצְאֹ֥ת הַגְּבֻ֖ל צְדָֽדָה׃

records.literal_gloss: From Hor the mountain you will mark out [to] Lebo-hamath, and will be [the] goings out of the border at Zedad.

en.L: From Mount Hor you will mark out [a line to] Lebo-hamath, and the end of the border will be at Zedad.
en.B: From Mount Hor mark it out to Lebo-hamath, and the border will reach out to Zedad.
en.R: From Mount Hor, draw it to Lebo-hamath and on to Zedad.

es.L: Desde el monte Hor {{plural_you:trazarán|trazaréis}} [una línea hasta] Lebo-jamat, y el término de la frontera estará en Zedad.
es.B: Desde el monte Hor {{plural_you:trácenla|trazadla}} hasta Lebo-jamat, y la frontera llegará hasta Zedad.
es.R: Desde el monte Hor, {{plural_you:trácenla|trazadla}} hasta Lebo-jamat y luego hasta Zedad.

fr.L: Depuis le mont Hor, vous tracerez [une ligne jusqu’à] Lebo-Hamath, et l’aboutissement de la frontière sera à Tsedad.
fr.B: Depuis le mont Hor, tracez-la jusqu’à Lebo-Hamath, et la frontière s’étendra jusqu’à Tsedad.
fr.R: Depuis le mont Hor, tracez-la jusqu’à Lebo-Hamath, puis jusqu’à Tsedad.

sw.L: Kutoka Mlima Hori mtapima [mstari hadi] Lebo-hamathi, na miisho ya mpaka itakuwa Sedadi.
sw.B: Kutoka Mlima Hori upimeni hadi Lebo-hamathi, na mpaka utafika hadi Sedadi.
sw.R: Kutoka Mlima Hori, uendelezeni hadi Lebo-hamathi, kisha hadi Sedadi.

vi.L: Từ núi Hô-rơ các ngươi sẽ vạch [một đường đến] Lê-bô Ha-mát, và điểm cuối của ranh giới sẽ ở Xê-đát.
vi.B: Từ núi Hô-rơ hãy vạch tiếp đến Lê-bô Ha-mát, và ranh giới sẽ chạy ra đến Xê-đát.
vi.R: Từ núi Hô-rơ, hãy vạch đường ấy đến Lê-bô Ha-mát rồi tiếp đến Xê-đát.

ko.L: 호르 산에서 르보하맛까지 너희가 [선을] 그을 것이요, 그 경계의 끝은 스닷이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 호르 산에서 르보하맛까지 선을 그어라. 경계는 스닷까지 이를 것이다.
ko.R: 호르 산에서 르보하맛을 지나 스닷까지 선을 그어라.

pt.L: Desde o monte Hor vocês traçarão [uma linha até] Lebo-Hamate, e o extremo da fronteira será em Zedade.
pt.B: Desde o monte Hor, tracem a linha até Lebo-Hamate, e a fronteira chegará até Zedade.
pt.R: Do monte Hor, tracem a linha até Lebo-Hamate e até Zedade.

decisions.choice: Lebo-hamath: a place name, or "the entrance of Hamath"
decisions.reason: As at 13:21, the words can be the name of a town or "the way into Hamath", the pass leading north into the land of Hamath in Syria. Either way it marks the northern edge of the land (1 Kings 8:65; Ezekiel 47:20).

decisions.choice: Zedad: a town on the far north-eastern border
decisions.reason: Zedad is named again on the northern border in Ezekiel 47:15. Its site is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: [a line to] (L), mark it out to (B)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

decisions.choice: "르보하맛" as one place name; "스닷"
decisions.reason: As Numbers 13:21 and Joshua 13:5 in Korean, following the English reading of a place name; the meaning decision gives "the entrance of Hamath" as the other reading.

source.text: וְיָצָ֤א הַגְּבֻל֙ זִפְרֹ֔נָה וְהָי֥וּ תוֹצְאֹתָ֖יו חֲצַ֣ר עֵינָ֑ן זֶֽה־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֥וּל צָפֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And will go out the border to Ziphron, and will be its goings out [at] Hazar-enan; this will be for you [the] border [of the] north.

en.L: And the border will go out to Ziphron, and its end will be at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern border.
en.B: The border will continue to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern border.
en.R: Then it will go on to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. That will be your border in the north.

es.L: Y la frontera saldrá hacia Zifrón, y su término estará en Hazar-enán. Esta será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera norte.
es.B: La frontera seguirá hasta Zifrón y terminará en Hazar-enán. Esta será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera norte.
es.R: Luego seguirá hasta Zifrón y terminará en Hazar-enán. Esa será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera por el norte.

fr.L: Et la frontière sortira vers Ziphron, et son aboutissement sera à Hatsar-Énan. Ce sera votre frontière du nord.
fr.B: La frontière continuera jusqu’à Ziphron et se terminera à Hatsar-Énan. Ce sera votre frontière nord.
fr.R: Ensuite, elle ira jusqu’à Ziphron et se terminera à Hatsar-Énan. Ce sera votre frontière au nord.

sw.L: Na mpaka utatokea hadi Zifroni, na miisho yake itakuwa Hasar-enani. Huu utakuwa mpaka wenu wa kaskazini.
sw.B: Mpaka utaendelea hadi Zifroni na kuishia Hasar-enani. Huu utakuwa mpaka wenu wa kaskazini.
sw.R: Kisha utaendelea hadi Zifroni na kuishia Hasar-enani. Huo ndio mpaka wenu upande wa kaskazini.

vi.L: Và ranh giới sẽ đi ra đến Xíp-rôn, và điểm cuối của nó sẽ ở Hát-sa-Ê-nan. Đây sẽ là ranh giới phía bắc của các ngươi.
vi.B: Ranh giới sẽ chạy tiếp đến Xíp-rôn và dừng lại ở Hát-sa-Ê-nan. Đây sẽ là ranh giới phía bắc của các ngươi.
vi.R: Rồi nó sẽ đi tiếp đến Xíp-rôn và dừng lại ở Hát-sa-Ê-nan. Đó là ranh giới phía bắc của các ngươi.

ko.L: 그리고 그 경계는 시브론으로 나가고, 그 끝은 하살에난이 될 것이다. 이것이 너희의 북쪽 경계가 될 것이다.
ko.B: 경계는 시브론으로 이어져 하살에난에서 끝날 것이다. 이것이 너희의 북쪽 경계가 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그다음에 경계는 시브론을 지나 하살에난에서 끝난다. 이것이 너희 땅의 북쪽 경계이다.

pt.L: E a fronteira sairá a Zifrom, e o seu extremo será em Hazar-Enã. Esta será a fronteira norte de vocês.
pt.B: A fronteira continuará até Zifrom e terminará em Hazar-Enã. Esta será a fronteira norte de vocês.
pt.R: Depois ela vai seguir até Zifrom e terminar em Hazar-Enã. Essa vai ser a fronteira de vocês no norte.

decisions.choice: Ziphron, Hazar-enan: the north-eastern end of the border
decisions.reason: Hazar-enan probably means "village of springs". It marks the corner where the northern border meets the eastern one (verse 10), as in Ezekiel 47:17 and 48:1. Ziphron is not named anywhere else, and neither site is known for certain.

decisions.choice: "시브론", "하살에난"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean forms of these names, written as one word like "하살아달" in verse 4.

decisions.choice: Zedade, Zifrom, Hazar-Enã; o seu extremo (L)
decisions.reason: The usual Brazilian forms of the names (Zedade in verse 8, and here): a final -d written "-de", -on "-om" and -an "-ã", as at 1:5. For the border's "goings out" (m2 at verse 4) Literal says "o seu extremo", one word each time it comes, as the English Literal says "its end"; "as suas saídas" would not read as the end of a line in Portuguese.

source.text: וְהִתְאַוִּיתֶ֥ם לָכֶ֖ם לִגְב֣וּל קֵ֑דְמָה מֵחֲצַ֥ר עֵינָ֖ן שְׁפָֽמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will mark out for yourselves for [the] border eastward from Hazar-enan to Shepham,

en.L: And you will mark out for yourselves [a line] for the eastern border from Hazar-enan to Shepham,
en.B: For your eastern border, mark out a line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
en.R: In the east, draw your border line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:trazarán|trazaréis}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [una línea] para la frontera oriental desde Hazar-enán hasta Sefam,
es.B: Para {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera oriental, {{plural_you:tracen|trazad}} una línea desde Hazar-enán hasta Sefam.
es.R: Al este, {{plural_you:tracen|trazad}} la línea de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} frontera desde Hazar-enán hasta Sefam.

fr.L: Et vous tracerez pour vous-mêmes [une ligne] pour la frontière de l’est, depuis Hatsar-Énan jusqu’à Shepham,
fr.B: Pour votre frontière est, tracez une ligne depuis Hatsar-Énan jusqu’à Shepham.
fr.R: À l’est, tracez la ligne de votre frontière depuis Hatsar-Énan jusqu’à Shepham.

sw.L: Nanyi mtajipimia [mstari] kwa ajili ya mpaka wa mashariki kutoka Hasar-enani hadi Shefamu,
sw.B: Kwa ajili ya mpaka wenu wa mashariki, pimeni mstari kutoka Hasar-enani hadi Shefamu.
sw.R: Upande wa mashariki, wekeni mstari wa mpaka wenu kuanzia Hasar-enani hadi Shefamu.

vi.L: Và các ngươi sẽ vạch cho mình [một đường] làm ranh giới phía đông từ Hát-sa-Ê-nan đến Sê-pham,
vi.B: Về ranh giới phía đông, hãy vạch một đường từ Hát-sa-Ê-nan đến Sê-pham.
vi.R: Ở phía đông, hãy vạch đường ranh giới từ Hát-sa-Ê-nan đến Sê-pham.

ko.L: 그리고 너희는 동쪽 경계로 하살에난에서 스밤까지 [선을] 그을 것이다.
ko.B: 동쪽 경계로는 하살에난에서 스밤까지 선을 그어라.
ko.R: 동쪽으로는 하살에난에서 스밤까지 경계선을 그어라.

pt.L: E vocês traçarão para si [uma linha] para a fronteira oriental, desde Hazar-Enã até Sefã,
pt.B: Para a fronteira oriental, tracem uma linha desde Hazar-Enã até Sefã.
pt.R: No leste, tracem a linha da fronteira desde Hazar-Enã até Sefã.

decisions.choice: you will mark out: draw a line
decisions.reason: The verb here is spelled like a verb that means "to desire", but that sense does not fit. It is a form with the same meaning as the verb in verses 7-8, to mark out a boundary, either a variant of that verb or a closely related one.

decisions.choice: [a line] (L), a line (B), draw your border line (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

source.text: וְיָרַ֨ד הַגְּבֻ֧ל מִשְּׁפָ֛ם הָרִבְלָ֖ה מִקֶּ֣דֶם לָעָ֑יִן וְיָרַ֣ד הַגְּב֔וּל וּמָחָ֛ה עַל־כֶּ֥תֶף יָם־כִּנֶּ֖רֶת קֵֽדְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will go down the border from Shepham [to] the Riblah, on [the] east of the Ain, and will go down the border and will strike against [the] shoulder of [the] Sea of Chinnereth eastward,

en.L: and the border will go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain; and the border will go down and strike against the slope of the Sea of Chinnereth on the east.
en.B: From Shepham the border will go down to Riblah, on the east side of Ain, and on down until it meets the slopes east of the Sea of Chinnereth.
en.R: From Shepham it will go down to Riblah, on the east side of Ain. Then it will go on down to the hills along the east shore of the Sea of Chinnereth (Lake Galilee).

es.L: y la frontera descenderá de Sefam a Riblá, al oriente de Aín; y la frontera descenderá y tocará la ladera del mar de Quinéret, al oriente.
es.B: Desde Sefam la frontera bajará hasta Riblá, al este de Aín, y seguirá bajando hasta encontrarse con las laderas al este del mar de Quinéret.
es.R: Desde Sefam bajará hasta Riblá, al este de Aín. Luego seguirá bajando hasta las colinas que bordean la orilla este del mar de Quinéret (el lago de Galilea).

fr.L: et la frontière descendra de Shepham à Ribla, à l’est d’Aïn ; et la frontière descendra et touchera le versant de la mer de Kinnéreth, à l’est.
fr.B: Depuis Shepham, la frontière descendra jusqu’à Ribla, à l’est d’Aïn, puis elle continuera à descendre jusqu’à atteindre les pentes à l’est de la mer de Kinnéreth.
fr.R: De Shepham, elle descendra jusqu’à Ribla, à l’est d’Aïn. Puis elle continuera à descendre jusqu’aux collines qui longent la rive est de la mer de Kinnéreth (le lac de Galilée).

sw.L: na mpaka utashuka kutoka Shefamu hadi Ribla, upande wa mashariki wa Aini; na mpaka utashuka na kugusa ubavu wa Bahari ya Kinerethi upande wa mashariki.
sw.B: Kutoka Shefamu mpaka utashuka hadi Ribla, upande wa mashariki wa Aini, na kuendelea kushuka hadi kufikia miteremko ya mashariki ya Bahari ya Kinerethi.
sw.R: Kutoka Shefamu utashuka hadi Ribla, upande wa mashariki wa Aini. Kisha utaendelea kushuka hadi kwenye vilima vilivyo kando ya pwani ya mashariki ya Bahari ya Kinerethi (Ziwa Galilaya).

vi.L: và ranh giới sẽ đi xuống từ Sê-pham đến Ríp-la, ở phía đông A-in; và ranh giới sẽ đi xuống và chạm đến sườn biển Ki-nê-rết về phía đông.
vi.B: Từ Sê-pham ranh giới sẽ đi xuống Ríp-la, ở phía đông A-in, rồi tiếp tục đi xuống cho đến khi chạm các sườn đồi phía đông biển Ki-nê-rết.
vi.R: Từ Sê-pham nó sẽ đi xuống Ríp-la, ở phía đông A-in. Rồi nó sẽ đi tiếp xuống đến các ngọn đồi dọc bờ phía đông của hồ Ki-nê-rết (hồ Ga-li-lê).

ko.L: 그리고 그 경계는 스밤에서 아인 동쪽 리블라로 내려가고, 그 경계는 내려가서 동쪽으로 긴네렛 바다의 비탈에 닿을 것이다.
ko.B: 경계는 스밤에서 아인 동쪽에 있는 리블라로 내려가고, 계속 내려가서 긴네렛 바다 동쪽 비탈에 닿을 것이다.
ko.R: 스밤에서 경계는 아인 동쪽에 있는 리블라로 내려간다. 그다음에 계속 내려가서 긴네렛 바다(갈릴리 호수) 동쪽 기슭의 언덕에 이른다.

pt.L: e a fronteira descerá desde Sefã até Ribla, ao leste de Aim; e a fronteira descerá e tocará a encosta do mar de Quinerete, a leste.
pt.B: De Sefã a fronteira descerá até Ribla, no lado leste de Aim, e continuará descendo até encontrar as encostas a leste do mar de Quinerete.
pt.R: De Sefã ela vai descer até Ribla, no lado leste de Aim. Depois vai continuar descendo até os morros ao longo da margem leste do mar de Quinerete (o mar da Galileia).

decisions.choice: Riblah and Ain: places on the eastern border
alternatives: Riblah in the land of Hamath
decisions.reason: Both names have "the" in front of them, "the Riblah" and "the Ain", and Ain means "spring". It is not certain whether this Riblah is the town in the land of Hamath where kings of Babylon and Egypt later held court (2 Kings 23:33; 25:6), which lies far to the north, or another place nearer the lake. The site of Ain is not known.

decisions.choice: strike against the shoulder: reach the slope
decisions.reason: "Shoulder" is used for the side of a hill or a ridge. The border runs down until it touches the high ground that rises from the east side of the lake.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Chinnereth: the lake later called the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Chinnereth was a town on the western shore (Joshua 19:35), and the lake took its name (Joshua 12:3; 13:27). In the Gospels it is the Sea of Galilee or the Lake of Gennesaret (Luke 5:1).

decisions.choice: (Lake Galilee)
decisions.reason: Readable adds the lake's later name, which most readers know.

decisions.choice: Riblah, Ain, without "the"
decisions.reason: English does not put "the" before a town's name, so the article is left out at every level; m1 notes it.

decisions.choice: le versant
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "shoulder" of a hill is the French "versant", its slope; "épaule" would not be understood of land.

decisions.choice: "biển Ki-nê-rết" (L, B), "hồ Ki-nê-rết (hồ Ga-li-lê)" (R)
decisions.reason: As Joshua 12:3 and 13:27 in Vietnamese; at R "hồ" (lake) says what the water is, and the bracket gives the name readers know from the Gospels.

decisions.choice: "비탈" for the "shoulder" (L, B); "긴네렛 바다", with "(갈릴리 호수)" at Readable
decisions.reason: Korean does not call a slope a "shoulder", so even Literal says "비탈", as the English Literal says "slope" (meaning decision). "긴네렛 바다" is the form Joshua 13:27 uses, with the same explanation at Readable.

decisions.choice: Sefã, Ribla, Aim; o mar de Quinerete; (o mar da Galileia) (R)
decisions.reason: The usual Brazilian forms of the names (Sefã in verse 10, and here), "qu" for ch before e. Readable adds the lake's later name as the Gospels give it in Portuguese, "o mar da Galileia" (m3), rather than the English Readable's "Lake Galilee", so that readers recognise the place they know from the Gospels.

source.text: וְיָרַ֤ד הַגְּבוּל֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔נָה וְהָי֥וּ תוֹצְאֹתָ֖יו יָ֣ם הַמֶּ֑לַח זֹאת֩ תִּהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֥ם הָאָ֛רֶץ לִגְבֻלֹתֶ֖יהָ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And will go down the border to the Jordan, and will be its goings out [at the] Sea of the Salt. This will be for you the land by its borders all around.

en.L: And the border will go down to the Jordan, and its end will be at the Salt Sea. This will be your land, by its borders all around.'"
en.B: Then the border will go down along the Jordan and end at the Dead Sea. This will be your land, with its borders on every side.'"
en.R: Then it will follow the Jordan River down to the Dead Sea. Those are the borders of your land on every side.'"

es.L: Y la frontera descenderá al Jordán, y su término estará en el mar Salado. Esta será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tierra, según sus fronteras alrededor.”»
es.B: Luego la frontera bajará a lo largo del Jordán y terminará en el mar Muerto. Esta será {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tierra, con sus fronteras por todos lados.”»
es.R: Después seguirá el río Jordán hacia abajo hasta el mar Muerto. Esas son las fronteras de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tierra por todos lados.”»

fr.L: Et la frontière descendra au Jourdain, et son aboutissement sera à la mer Salée. Tel sera votre pays, selon ses frontières tout autour.” »
fr.B: Puis la frontière descendra le long du Jourdain et se terminera à la mer Morte. Tel sera votre pays, avec ses frontières de tous côtés.” »
fr.R: Ensuite, elle suivra le Jourdain jusqu’à la mer Morte. Voilà les frontières de votre pays de tous les côtés.” »

sw.L: Na mpaka utashuka hadi Yordani, na miisho yake itakuwa Bahari ya Chumvi. Hii itakuwa nchi yenu kwa mipaka yake pande zote.'"
sw.B: Kisha mpaka utashuka kufuata Yordani na kuishia Bahari Mfu. Hii itakuwa nchi yenu, pamoja na mipaka yake pande zote.'"
sw.R: Kisha utafuata Mto Yordani kushuka hadi Bahari Mfu. Hiyo ndiyo mipaka ya nchi yenu pande zote.'"

vi.L: Và ranh giới sẽ đi xuống đến sông Giô-đanh, và điểm cuối của nó sẽ ở Biển Muối. Đây sẽ là xứ của các ngươi, theo các ranh giới của nó chung quanh.'"
vi.B: Rồi ranh giới sẽ đi xuống dọc theo sông Giô-đanh và dừng lại ở Biển Chết. Đó sẽ là xứ của các ngươi, với ranh giới bốn phía.'"
vi.R: Rồi nó sẽ theo sông Giô-đanh xuống đến Biển Chết. Đó là ranh giới bốn phía của xứ các ngươi.'"

ko.L: 그리고 그 경계는 요단으로 내려가고, 그 끝은 염해가 될 것이다. 이것이 사방 경계대로의 너희 땅이 될 것이다.'"
ko.B: 그다음에 경계는 요단강을 따라 내려가서 사해에서 끝날 것이다. 이것이 사방 경계로 둘러싸인 너희 땅이 될 것이다.'"
ko.R: 그다음에 경계는 요단강을 따라 사해까지 내려간다. 이것이 너희 땅의 사방 경계이다.'"

pt.L: E a fronteira descerá até o Jordão, e o seu extremo será no mar Salgado. Esta será a terra de vocês, segundo as suas fronteiras ao redor.'"
pt.B: Depois a fronteira descerá ao longo do Jordão e terminará no mar Morto. Esta será a terra de vocês, com as suas fronteiras de todos os lados.'"
pt.R: Depois ela vai acompanhar o rio Jordão até o mar Morto. Essas são as fronteiras da terra de vocês, de todos os lados.'"

decisions.choice: the Jordan: the eastern border
decisions.reason: From the Sea of Chinnereth the border follows the Jordan down to the Dead Sea, where the southern border began (verse 3), and so the line closes. The land east of the Jordan, already given to two and a half tribes (32:33; verses 14-15), lies outside the land of Canaan described here; this is why the eastern tribes had to show they belonged to Israel (Joshua 22:24-27).

decisions.choice: this will be your land: the summary that closes the description
decisions.reason: The words answer verse 2: "this is the land ... the land of Canaan by its borders". All that lies between the four lines is the land given to Israel.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea; the Jordan River (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 3. Readable calls the Jordan a river.

records.literal_gloss: And commanded Moses [the] sons of Israel, saying, This [is] the land that you will receive as inheritance by lot, which commanded Yahweh to give to [the] nine tribes and [the] half of the tribe.

en.L: And Moses commanded the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, "This [is] the land which you will receive as an inheritance by lot, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded to give to the nine tribes and the half of the tribe.
en.B: Moses gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this command: "This is the land you are to divide among yourselves by lot as your inheritance. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded that it be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
en.R: Moses told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "This is the land you will receive as your own. You will divide it by drawing lots. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded that it be given to the nine tribes and to half of the tribe of Manasseh.

es.L: Y mandó Moisés a los hijos de Israel, diciendo: «Esta [es] la tierra que {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} en herencia por sorteo, la cual {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha mandado dar a las nueve tribus y a la mitad de la tribu.
es.B: Moisés dio esta orden a los israelitas: «Esta es la tierra que {{plural_you:se repartirán|os repartiréis}} por sorteo como herencia. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha mandado que se dé a las nueve tribus y a la media tribu.
es.R: Moisés les dijo a los israelitas: «Esta es la tierra que {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} como {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}. La {{plural_you:repartirán|repartiréis}} por sorteo. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha mandado que se dé a las nueve tribus y a la mitad de la tribu de Manasés.

fr.L: Et Moïse commanda aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, en disant : « Voici le pays que vous recevrez en héritage par le sort, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a ordonné de donner aux neuf tribus et à la moitié de la tribu.

sw.L: Naye Musa akawaamuru wana wa Israeli, akisema, "Hii [ndiyo] nchi mtakayoirithi kwa kura, ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameamuru wapewe makabila tisa na nusu ya kabila.

vi.R: Môi-se bảo dân Y-sơ-ra-ên: "Đây là xứ anh em sẽ nhận làm đất riêng. Anh em sẽ chia nhau xứ ấy bằng cách bắt thăm. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền phải ban xứ này cho chín chi tộc và nửa chi tộc Ma-na-se.

pt.L: E Moisés ordenou aos filhos de Israel, dizendo: "Esta [é] a terra que vocês receberão como herança por sorte, a qual {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} ordenou dar às nove tribos e à meia tribo.
pt.B: Moisés deu esta ordem aos israelitas: "Esta é a terra que vocês vão repartir entre si por sorteio, como herança. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} ordenou que ela seja dada às nove tribos e à meia tribo.

decisions.choice: by lot: the shares decided by casting lots
decisions.reason: The land was to be shared out by lot (26:55-56; 33:54), so that the choice of which tribe received which region was left to the LORD, not to the leaders (Proverbs 16:33). Joshua 14:2 and 18:10 tell how it was done.

decisions.choice: you will receive as an inheritance: take as your own possession, each tribe its share
decisions.reason: The verb form means to receive something as one's inheritance, here with the sense of taking possession of it among themselves, tribe by tribe. The same form is used in 32:18 and 33:54.

decisions.choice: the nine tribes and the half of the tribe: the tribes that settle west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Twelve tribes share the land, with Joseph counted as two (Ephraim and Manasseh) and Levi given no tribal land (18:20-24; 35:1-8). Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh settle east of the Jordan (chapter 32; verses 14-15), so nine and a half tribes remain for Canaan. The half-tribe is the other half of Manasseh (Joshua 14:1-3; 17:1-6).

decisions.choice: half of the tribe of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Readable names the tribe, as verse 14 does (m3).

decisions.choice: Moses speaks to the people as "các ngươi" at L and "anh em" at B and R
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form for Moses addressing Israel: "anh em" makes him one of the people he speaks to, as in Exodus; L keeps the plain plural "you" of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "chi tộc" for tribe (matteh)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word, used through Numbers; Joshua's Vietnamese has "chi phái" for the same word.

decisions.choice: Moses speaking to Israel: plain style (해라체) with "너희" at Literal and Balanced; formal polite style (합쇼체) with "여러분" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for Exodus to Deuteronomy sets Moses' speeches to the people. Recorded once for Numbers 34-36.

decisions.choice: por sorte (L); por sorteio (B, R)
decisions.reason: As 26:55 has it in Portuguese: Literal says "por sorte", the old phrase for a share decided by lot (m1), and Balanced and Readable "por sorteio", which a modern reader cannot take for "by luck".

decisions.choice: a meia tribo (L, B); a meia tribo de Manassés (R)
decisions.reason: "A meia tribo" is the Portuguese phrase for the half of Manasseh that settles apart (m3), as the book says it from chapter 32; Readable names the tribe, as the English Readable does, keeping the same phrase rather than the English "half of the tribe".

pt.L: Porque a tribo dos filhos dos rubenitas, segundo as suas famílias, e a tribo dos filhos dos gaditas, segundo as suas famílias, receberam [a sua parte], e a meia tribo de Manassés recebeu a sua herança.

pt.R: A tribo de Rúben e a tribo de Gade, família por família, já receberam a sua terra, e a meia tribo de Manassés também.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the land is shared by only nine and a half tribes
alternatives: a note by the narrator outside the speech
decisions.reason: Verses 14-15 explain verse 13. They may be the end of Moses' words to the people or a note added by the narrator; either way they give the reason, and the sense does not change.

decisions.choice: have taken: their share is already settled
decisions.reason: The verb "have taken" is said twice, once at the start and once at the end of the long subject. The two and a half tribes have already been given their land east of the Jordan by Moses (32:33), even though their men must still cross and fight with the rest (32:20-22, 29).

decisions.choice: by the house of their fathers: family by family
decisions.reason: The "house of the fathers" is the extended family traced through the male line, a unit within the clan (1:2). Even the eastern land was given out family by family.

decisions.choice: [theirs]
decisions.reason: The first "have taken" has no object in Hebrew until the end of the verse; Literal brackets "theirs" so it can stand where it is.

decisions.choice: one verb, "have already received"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "have received" once and add "already", which gives the force of the past tense (m2).

decisions.choice: "조상의 집대로" (L); "집안별로" (B, R) for "by the house of their fathers"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets the father's house: "조상의 집" at Literal, "집안" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: receberam [a sua parte] ... recebeu a sua herança (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "have taken" twice, in the plural both times (m2). Portuguese makes the second verb agree with its nearer subject, "a meia tribo ... recebeu", since a plural after a singular subject reads as a mistake; Literal brackets "a sua parte" as the English brackets "theirs". "Os rubenitas" and "os gaditas" are the Portuguese names of the clans, formed like "os levitas"; the Literal's "filhos" needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: apportion for you: give you the land as an inheritance, sharing it out
decisions.reason: The verb is the one from which "inheritance" comes. With "for you" it means to put the people in possession of the land by dividing it among them. The same task is given to the tribal leaders in verse 18 and summed up in verse 29.

decisions.choice: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun: the leaders after Moses

decisions.choice: for you: the people as a whole

decisions.choice: divide up the land and give each of you your share

decisions.choice: Caleb son of Jephunneh: the faithful scout
decisions.reason: Caleb was Judah's scout, who urged the people to go up and take the land (13:6, 30; 14:6-9). He and Joshua were the only men of their generation spared to enter it (14:24, 30, 38; 26:65). He now helps to divide the land he had trusted the LORD to give.

decisions.choice: the order of the tribes: roughly from south to north
decisions.reason: The list in verses 19-28 runs in pairs, mostly in the order of the tribes' later land from south to north: Judah and Simeon, Benjamin and Dan, then Manasseh and Ephraim, Zebulun and Issachar, Asher and Naphtali (Joshua 15-19).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end
decisions.reason: Verses 19-28 are one list in Hebrew. Literal and Balanced end each name with a comma and close the list at verse 28; Readable gives each name its own sentence.

decisions.choice: Names of the ten leaders in the usual Protestant forms, father first: "여분네의 아들 갈렙", "암미훗의 아들 스므엘", "기슬론의 아들 엘리닷", "요글리의 아들 북기", "에봇의 아들 한니엘", "십단의 아들 그므엘", "바르낙의 아들 엘리사반", "앗산의 아들 발디엘", "슬로미의 아들 아히훗", "암미훗의 아들 브다헬"
decisions.reason: The forms Korean Protestant readers know, as Numbers 1 and 13 already list names in Korean. Each entry ends with a comma at every level, Readable included, so the list reads as one sentence closed at verse 28.

decisions.choice: Calebe, filho de Jefoné, and the forms of verses 20-28
decisions.reason: The ten leaders in the usual Brazilian forms, on the pattern of 1:5 and 13:4 ("s" for sh, "f" for ph, "qu" for k and ch before e and i, a final -an "-ã", -on "-om", -d "-de"): Calebe, filho de Jefoné (Judá); Semuel, filho de Amiúde (Simeão); Elidade, filho de Quislom (Benjamim); Buqui, filho de Jogli (Dã); Haniel, filho de Éfode (Manassés); Quemuel, filho de Siftã (Efraim); Elisafã, filho de Parnaque (Zebulom); Paltiel, filho de Azã (Issacar); Aiúde, filho de Selomi (Aser); Pedael, filho de Amiúde (Naftali). "Semuel" is kept apart from "Samuel", as the English keeps "Shemuel" (m1 at verse 20); "Amiúde" is the form of 1:10. Literal and Balanced end each entry with a semicolon, not the English comma, because each entry already has a comma before "filho de"; Readable gives each name its own sentence, as 13:4-15 does.

decisions.choice: Ephod: a personal name
decisions.reason: Hanniel's father has the same name as the priest's garment, the ephod (Exodus 28:6), but here it is simply a man's name.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means the whole line descended from Joseph; Balanced and Readable say "descendants", which already includes everyone, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: "Ê-phót", capitalised, for the personal name
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the priest's garment, written "áo ê-phót" in lower case; the capital and the absence of "áo" show that a man is meant.

decisions.choice: a closing summary in the narrator's voice
alternatives: the last words of the LORD's speech
decisions.reason: The verse speaks of the LORD in the third person and sums up verses 17-28. It is best read as the narrator's closing line, like 36:13, though the LORD sometimes speaks of himself by name and it could end his speech.

decisions.choice: to apportion: to put the people in possession of their inheritance
decisions.reason: The verb here means to give someone a share as their inheritance. The men named are to see that every tribe, clan and family receives its portion of Canaan, as is done in Joshua 14-19.

decisions.choice: gave the task of dividing
decisions.reason: Readable puts "commanded to apportion" as giving the men a task, which is what the command did.
